claims.text: Set the cable pulley at its highest position (above head height) with a straight bar attached.

quotes.text: Place the cable pulley at the highest position, use a straight bar attachment, and grip the bar firmly in both hands.
Stand facing the cable machine and position the cable attachment at a height above your head.

claims.text: Grip the bar overhand (palms down), hands about shoulder-width, with a full grip: thumbs wrapped round the bar.

quotes.text: grasp it firmly with a full grip (thumbs clasped around the handle or rope).
The subject then stood in front of the triceps push-down machine and held the straight-bar with both hands in the pronated position at shoulder width.

claims.text: Stand with feet hip-width apart or in a staggered (walking) stance.

quotes.text: Position your feet hip-width apart or in a staggered-stance (walking) position.

claims.text: Keep the torso tall and braced. A slight forward lean is fine if it comes from the hips, not from arching the back, so the bar clears the body at the bottom.

quotes.text: Stiffen (“brace”) your abdominal muscles to stabilize your spine with a natural arch in your low back, keeping your torso aligned vertically with the floor and maintaining this position throughout the exercise.
with his torso slightly leaned forward to ensure that the bar did not touch the body during full extension.
If you need to lean slightly forward, make sure to tilt from your hips rather than arching your back.

claims.text: The elbows stay right next to the sides for the whole set.

quotes.text: Continue pressing the weight with your elbows right next to your side while maintaining a neutral position with your wrists until your elbows become fully extended
Remember to keep your elbows close to your sides, and locked in.

claims.text: Elbows moving forward is the fault to watch: it brings in the lats and takes work off the triceps.

quotes.text: It is important to monitor the forward movement of your elbows as this recruits from your lats (back muscles) and reduces the emphasis on the triceps.

claims.text: Start (top) position: elbows bent and at the sides, bar at about upper-chest level; on the way up, stop before the elbows start to drift forward.

quotes.text: moving the handle / rope upwards until your elbows begin to drift forward from the mid-line of your trunk (around upper chest level).
Start with the bar at the upper-chest level and your elbows bent and close to your sides.

claims.text: End (bottom) position: arms fully straight, without snapping the elbows into a hard lockout.

quotes.text: until your elbows become fully extended, (do not allow them to "lock out" in full extension).
Straighten the arms completely before bending the elbows to return to the starting position.

claims.text: The wrists stay neutral, in line with the forearms, throughout.

quotes.text: arms postioned firmly by sides and wrists in neutral positon (i.e., aligned with your forearms).  This arm and wrist position should be maintained throughout the exercise.

claims.text: Keep the shoulders pulled down and back through the set.

quotes.text: Depress and retract your scapulae (pull shoulders back and down) and attempt to hold this position throughout the exercise.

claims.text: Leaning too far forward or arching the back strains the lower back and moves work off the triceps.

quotes.text: Some people tend to lean too far forward or arch their back, which can put unnecessary strain on the lower back and shift the focus away from the triceps.

claims.text: Tempo (up = working phase, the press down; down = return): press in about 1 s, pause briefly at the bottom, return slowly in about 2 s. ACSM advises moderate speed (1-2 s each way).

quotes.text: Pause momentarily then slowly return to your starting position, allowing your elbows to flex (bend) in a slow, controlled manner
at a moderate contraction velocity (1-2 s CON; 1-2 s ECC)

claims.text: Breathe out as you press the bar down.

quotes.text: Gently exhale and slowly extend your elbows, pressing the handle / rope down towards the floor.

claims.text: Only the elbow joint moves; the body stays still and doesn't add momentum or body weight.

quotes.text: The only movement that should happen is in your elbow joint, so keep your body still and try not to create excessive momentum.
the assistant also ensured that the subject did not use his body weight to move the bar.

claims.text: The pushdown is a full-range elbow extension exercise; all three heads of the triceps were measured working in it.

quotes.text: The triceps push-down exercise is an isotonic exercise that involves the full ROM of elbow extensors against a load.
surface electromyography (sEMG) signals were recorded from the lateral, long and medial heads of the TB.

claims.text: Too much weight leads to momentum and can lead to injury; pick a weight you can move with control.

quotes.text: This not only reduces the effectiveness of the exercise but can also lead to injury. Make sure to pick a weight where you can do the movement with control.
quotes.where: Common mistakes, using too much weight

claims.text: Heavy, low-rep pushdowns feel uncomfortable in the elbows for many people; lighter weights for more reps can ease this.

quotes.text: For the triceps pushdown, using heavy weights and low reps feels uncomfortable in the elbows for many people, and using lighter weights and doing more reps can alleviate this.

claims.text: Load progression: add 2-10% load once you can do one or two reps more than the target number.

quotes.text: When training at a specific RM load, it is recommended that 2-10% increase in load be applied when the individual can perform the current workload for one to two repetitions over the desired number.

plate.viewWhy: The elbow bends front-to-back and the key fault, elbows drifting forward (c6), plus trunk lean (c4, c11) only read side-on. Census view is side.
plate.equipment: Cable column with the pulley at its top position (above head height), straight bar on the cable (c1). Floor line.
plate.start: Standing facing the stack, feet hip-width or staggered (c3); torso tall or slightly leaned from the hips (c4); elbows bent at the sides, bar at about upper-chest level (c7); wrists neutral (c9); shoulders down and back (c10).
plate.end: Arms fully straight with the bar in front of the thighs, elbows still at the sides and not hard-locked (c5, c8); torso unchanged (c14).

checkpoints.label: Elbows pinned
checkpoints.what: Upper arms stay against the sides; only the forearms move.

checkpoints.label: Tall torso
checkpoints.what: Torso upright or slightly tilted from the hips, back not arched.

checkpoints.label: Neutral wrists
checkpoints.what: Hands in line with the forearms from top to bottom.

mistake.what: Elbows drifting forward as the bar comes up (and swinging forward to start the press).
mistake.why: ACE names it as the fault to monitor: it brings in the lats and takes load off the triceps.

grip.type: Overhand (palms down) on a straight bar, full grip.
grip.wrist: Neutral, in line with the forearm, for the whole set.

setup.step: Set the pulley at the top position and attach a straight bar.
Grip the bar overhand, hands shoulder-width, thumbs wrapped.
Stand facing the machine, feet hip-width or staggered.
Brace, shoulders down and back, elbows at your sides with the bar at upper-chest level.
Pick a weight you can move with control.

posture.point: Elbows stay right next to your sides.
Torso tall; any lean comes from the hips, not an arched back.
Straighten the arms fully at the bottom without a hard lockout.
Return only until the elbows start to move forward.

handlingMistakes.fix: Keep the elbows at your sides; stop the return at upper-chest level.

handlingMistakes.mistake: Leaning over the bar or arching the back.
handlingMistakes.fix: Stand taller; tilt only from the hips; go lighter.

handlingMistakes.mistake: Weight too heavy, moved with momentum.
handlingMistakes.fix: Go lighter and move with control.

rows.means: The triceps are doing the work.
Usually means the elbows are drifting forward.
rows.fix: Pin the elbows to your sides.

rows.means: Usually means you are leaning too far or arching.
Heavy, low-rep sets often feel this way.
rows.fix: Use a lighter weight for more reps.

risks.risk: Leaning or arching strains the lower back.
Heavy loads feel uncomfortable in the elbows for many people.
Too much weight moved with momentum can lead to injury.

zooms.right: Overhand full grip, thumbs wrapped, hands in line with the forearms.
zooms.wrong: Wrists bent back over the bar.

zooms.right: Elbows against the sides at the top of the return.
zooms.wrong: Elbows drifted forward, upper arms swung up.

libraryDiff.why: triceps primary is sourced (c15). exercises.json lists forearms as secondary; no source I read names the forearms for the bar pushdown (StrengthLog lists only the triceps), so it is kept unchanged and flagged unsourced rather than removed without evidence.
